source: User-supplied ONiO characterization in the project conversation, 2026-10-05–2026-10-06; not independently verified against a revision-specific datasheet.
limitations: User-provided baseline, not manufacturer-verified electrical data. Silicon revision, package, measurement rail and temperature are unspecified.
Runnable model has a logical power input only. User-confirmed VMAIN storage capability is recorded separately; physical package pin numbers are unknown.
Whole-device radio states include a sleeping CPU. Do not add CPU or sleep baseline power to them.
CPU run powers use 22 µW/MHz with no added fixed baseline; this remains a model assumption.
Power is held constant within the stated range; voltage-dependent curves and the 3 V upper limit are not enforced by the current engine.
Transition durations require explicit timeline events; they are not automatically inserted by the engine.
BLE 2M/coded operation and TX powers other than 0 dBm remain uncharacterized.
Harvesting, storage, cold start, output rails and brownout/restart behavior remain outside this baseline.

vmain_storage.source: User statements in the project conversation, 2026-10-06: ONiO.zero supports energy storage attached at VMAIN, using a capacitor, supercapacitor or battery. The user separately confirmed a VMAIN minimum operating voltage of 250 mV and a maximum operating voltage of 3.3 V.
vmain_storage.note: Capability, vendor port name and 0.25–3.3 V operating range are user supplied. Package mapping and charge/discharge behavior remain uncharacterized. The maximum operating voltage is not yet a characterized charging stop voltage. Battery charging depends on chemistry and an explicitly characterized charging path. The current runnable part remains a consumption-only load and does not simulate VMAIN storage.
